pf.services.capacity: One estimator or product advisor per booking; one install crew per job at a time; large glass needs two people; the showroom's design table is saved with long sessions

pf.services.nobody_home: Estimates and tune-ups: nobody needs to be home if the gate is open. Install days: an adult on the booking is reachable by phone, because a room is open to the weather while the crew works.
pf.services.online: No video or phone window consult: it uses the samples at the showroom
pf.services.smallest_job: A switch the owner sets: the smallest job taken, with smaller requests pointed elsewhere (the example takes no order for fewer than 2 windows).

stop.words: gas smell, hissing near a gas line, sparking or smoking wires, a carbon monoxide alarm
stop.says: Leave the house now. Then call 911 and the gas or power company.
stop.booking: no booking; a new request must say the home was made safe

stop.words: glass has broken and someone is bleeding, a large pane is falling from its frame, or a frame is coming out of the wall
stop.says: Keep everyone back from the glass, press a clean cloth on any bleeding, and call 911 if anyone is badly hurt.

steps_then_go_on.says: Tape a crack on both sides if you can, and keep children and pets away from it. We'll look at it first.

steps_then_go_on.words: worry about lead paint or old putty around old window frames
steps_then_go_on.says: Don't scrape or sand the old frames. We'll test first.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; testing becomes a first step

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about a window's strength or fire rating, or about changing the size of an opening in a wall, go to the business's own line

pf.visit.check_in: Estimate visit: the check-in code at the door. Each work day: that day's code, or the lockbox and a start photo when nobody is home. Showroom: the code at the desk.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The estimator measures every opening (width, height, depth), checks the frames, walls and trim, and photographs; the written quote follows within 3 business days, good for 30 days
pf.visit.changes: A written change order, priced and signed by both, before any changed work. A different size or style after the order, or rotted wood found behind the trim, is priced this way.
pf.visit.outside_checks: A permit inspection after the install, where the permit requires it
pf.visit.done: The walk-through and punch list (every window opens, locks and seals), then DONE on the last install day; the care notes go with it
pf.visit.studio_done: DONE after the consult, with the product advisor's notes and the picks saved for the estimate
pf.visit.before_photos: Each opening inside and out, the walls and trim, and floors and furniture nearby that could be hit

pf.money.estimate: The example's $89 estimate visit is credited to the job; billed only if no contract follows. A free estimate is the safe start.
pf.money.no_money_before_contract: On project work, nothing is taken before the contract is signed by everyone on the deed
pf.money.deposit: Only after signing; the cap comes from the state's form, which may allow more up front for made-to-order items
pf.money.kept_apart: Money paid before the work is kept apart or bonded where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.stages: Each stage is billed only when it's done and any check has passed: the start (the order), the install, the finish. Never ahead of the work
pf.money.last_payment: After the walk-through and punch list
pf.money.change_orders: Added to the next stage bill
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe, for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears. A check also works: the crew lead texts 'paid check'.
pf.money.tax: Tax on materials and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.studio: The 3D window preview's $55 is credited to the job if Alex signs; the $20 missed-consult fee only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: Contract, change order and permit papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home is never the one who lets the crew in

pf.staff.roles: Crew leads (Dale, Beto): estimates, quotes and running the job, with the crew. Product advisors (Anya, Wren) at the showroom.
pf.staff.licenses: The company holds the contractor registration or license. Where the state's form also licenses each person, each one may add a number (optional, shown as given, not checked by Rosie). Subcontractors hold their own, as the business says.
pf.staff.lead_safe: A certified renovator on each job in an older home, where lead-safe rules apply
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes and change orders over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another crew lead may take an estimate visit; a job keeps its crew lead unless Sam moves it

pf.rules.contract: A written contract for project work where the state's rules require one, signed by everyone on the deed and by the business before any money
pf.rules.contract_parts: The parts the state's form lists (license number, dates, price, deposit, cancel notice, any lien notice)
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one; work and orders wait for it
pf.rules.permits: Pulled by the license holder in the business's name, never the homeowner's
pf.rules.change_orders: Written and signed by both before the changed work
pf.rules.final: The punch list and any permit sign-off before the last payment
pf.rules.lien_waivers: Lien waivers from the business and its subcontractors with the last payment, where the state's rules provide them
pf.rules.show: The license number on the listing, the quote, the contract and the receipt, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.warranty: 1 year on workmanship (the example's); makers' warranties on frames and glass, including the glass seal. The contract says what is covered.

pf.edges.weather: Rain, strong wind or freezing cold on install day: the crew doesn't open a wall; the day moves, with no fee
pf.edges.factory_late: A factory order is late: the install day moves and the owner is told the new day, with no fee; or an in-stock item with the owner's yes
pf.edges.wrong_size: A window that doesn't fit because of the business's own measure is remade at the business's cost; a size the owner changes after the order is a change order
pf.edges.glass_broken: Glass broken in delivery or on site: remade, a new day, no fee to the customer
pf.edges.hidden_conditions: Rot behind the trim, an out-of-square opening or a weak lintel found when the old window comes out: a change order before the fix
pf.edges.lead_or_asbestos: Lead paint, or old putty that may hold asbestos: lead-safe or licensed work first, by its own quote; the start moves
pf.edges.made_to_order: Made-to-order glass and frames can't be returned once in production; the contract says so, and the cancel window comes first
pf.edges.permit_late: The install moves with no fee; Alex is told
pf.edges.inspection_fails: The crew fixes it and it's checked again; the last bill waits
pf.edges.cancel_after_window: Sam and the customer settle it; Rosie moves no money on its own
pf.edges.nobody_home: Estimates and tune-ups with the gate open, with start and end photos
pf.edges.over_license_limit: Not offered, and the owner is told why
pf.edges.walk_through_dispute: Goes to Sam; the last bill waits
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

notes:
Started from contractor (pattern: project; refitted that morning, not edited): an estimate visit, a written quote, then a contract and stage bills. Facts: documents, stages, photos, extrawork, firststeps, multiday, banktransfer; switch cancelright in flow B only (work sold at the customer's place); arrive A a set start, B a 2-hour window; cutoff 24 hours before.
Flow B main path visit|none|bill: the booking is the $89 estimate visit, credited to the job; Dale's written quote; the contract signed by everyone on the deed; $1,920 to start, $5,760 when the windows are installed and sealed, $1,920 at the finish (a $9,600 window replacement). The $89 keeps the master's numbers true; a free estimate is the owner's choice (pf.money).
B money paths: visit|none|bill, visit|none|own, visit|card|bill, photos|deposit|bill (Door glass unit, $640 from photos, a $160 deposit, a $480 rest). Left out: list paths. Door tune-up ($179) and Window tune-up ($150) are in pf.services, but the master's booking cards name one list service, so a list path would show the wrong name (MASTER).
Flow A is Sam's second company, Lee Glass Studio, a window showroom (the master's Lee's Barbershop). Main path list|card|counter: a $35 window consult with Anya, a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee, paid at the showroom desk. The other three: list|none|counter, list|full|none (3D window preview, $55, credited to the job if Alex signs), list|deposit|counter (window and door package, $140, $40 deposit).
Flow A has no video or phone consult: the window consult uses the sample frames and glass at the showroom (the A4-01 video branch is hidden because the fact `video` is not listed).
Own steps: A8-x01 (the window consult offers the estimate visit at home), B8-x06 to B8-x08 (the second measure and the factory order go first, with any permit; a late factory order moves the install day with no fee; a re-measure that is 2 inches off holds the order until the size is settled) and B8-x11 / B8-x12 (rotted wood found under two sills: a change order first, signed by both).
Windows and doors are made to order: nothing is ordered inside the cancel window, every opening is measured twice, the order takes about five weeks (so the work days are in December, Mon Dec 7 to Tue Dec 8 or Mon Dec 14 to Tue Dec 15), a factory delay moves the day with no fee, and a made-to-order item can't be returned once the factory starts it (pf.edges made_to_order). Older homes get lead-safe setup (pf.license lead_safe). Stop words: a gas smell or sparking wires; broken glass that has hurt someone, a large pane falling from its frame, a frame coming out of the wall. A cracked pane that has not fallen and fogged glass are go-ons ('tape it, keep children and pets back').
Dates run forward: cancel window ends Tue Oct 27; the measure and order to-do Wed Oct 28 ('due this week, so the windows arrive before the first install day, Mon Dec 7'); the re-measure Thu Oct 29; a late factory order Fri Dec 4 with new install days Mon Dec 14 / Mon Dec 21; the change order Tue Dec 8.
Booking choices: B timing settime, times window; A times setstart. Nothing is sent now (S2-30 'Yes' branch off, no `sentnow` fact), so nobody is on call. After turning it off, the joined text was searched for the opposite claim: S2-30's 'Neither window installation nor the showroom takes jobs sent now' and S1-21's 'Jobs sent now: None: every job is booked ahead' are re-worded; the other 'sent now' lines are the master's general rules for work that does send.
Plug-in splits kept whole (splitsKept): A7-15; B5-34, B7-55, B8-58, B8-69 (as the parent).
Self-checks: (1) the opposite-claim search above; (2) every example message was searched for this work's stop words (they appear only in the danger-words line and the plug-in); (3) B3-11 and B3-18 read as one Spanish conversation: the caller describes a go-on case, is asked about injury and gas, answers no, and gets the safety steps.
Names: Dale and Beto are the crew leads (the master's Jordan and Casey), Anya and Wren the product advisors (Riley and Avery). None of them is a master customer's name. Addresses: 88 Foundry Ln (the company), 14 Canal St (the showroom), 72 Alder Way (Alex). License numbers use an obviously fake format (EX-1042, EX-2087, EX-3150, EX-4216, EX-5309), also in place of the master's S2-21 person licenses.
Every state rule is a switch from the state's form: the license and its job-size limit, the written contract and its parts, the deposit cap, money kept apart, the cancel window, permits, lien waivers, what must be shown. No state, city or number from one.
